note: Code IS the source column name: data/CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020.R does select(starts_with('PANAS')) (tidyselect, case-insensitive) + pivot_longer on ex.dataset.csv, whose headers are panas_1..panas_20 -- no rename, no positional step. But those columns carry no text at any level (plain semicolon CSV, no variable/value labels, zero non-ASCII bytes in the file; retest.data.oasis.odsis.sav and data.pa.aft.imp.Rds contain no PANAS variables), so mapping_basis is reconstructed, not data_labels. The 20 codes are reconstructed as the canonical Watson, Clark & Tellegen (1988) PANAS in its printed order. Grounds: the study's own CZ_short_OASIS_ODSIS.Rmd scores positive affect as panas_{1,3,5,9,10,12,14,16,17,19} and negative as panas_{2,4,6,7,8,11,13,15,18,20} -- exactly the canonical PA/NA positions, 1 of C(20,10)=184,756 splits -- and the live data reproduce that block structure (19/20 items correlate more with their own block; the exception, panas_12 = alert, is the item the authors themselves flag in an Rmd comment as tied to negative emotionality). See verification/verify sidecars; status PARTIAL. TEXT: the administration was Czech and no Czech PANAS wording exists in the deposit or the paper (Section 2.2.5 names the instrument, says 'Respondents rated one-word items ... on a scale from 1 to 5', and quotes only 'determined' and 'attentive' in the Discussion); so the shipped adjectives are Watson et al.'s canonical English: text_source=translated_substitute, language=Czech, _translated columns omitted (backfill signal). OPTIONS: the paper prints no anchor labels, only '1 to 5' with 'Higher scores indicated higher levels of the respective affects'; the five canonical PANAS anchors ('very slightly or not at all', 'a little', 'moderately', 'quite a bit', 'extremely') are imported from Watson et al. 1988 for all five points, not taken from this study. Direction checked, not assumed: in the OSF raw file (identical to the live table: 1458 rows, per-item means equal to 4e-15) the canonical P total correlates +0.126 with scored RSES and the N total +0.447 with scored BFI-N, so resp ascends with affect in both blocks; no PANAS item is reverse-keyed and the table stores raw responses. INSTRUCTIONS left blank: neither the paper nor the deposit reproduces the instruction paragraph; the Rmd's prose describes the reference period as the past week ('negative emotions experienced in past week'), which is not a canonical Watson time frame, so the canonical paragraph was not imported. SOURCE DEFECT (paper, not response data): the Rmd computes PANAS_P as rowSums(across(starts_with(c('panas_1', ...)))), which also captures panas_11/13/15/18 (four NA items), so the paper's Table 4 PANAS-P (28.83, SD 9.77; r=0.61 with PANAS-N) is a 14-item sum. From the live codes the Rmd selection gives 28.92 (SD 9.89) and r(P,N)=0.64 (Pearson), vs 21.34 (SD 8.02) and r=0.40 (Spearman, raw) for the correct 10-item PA sum; PANAS-N (18.33, SD 7.65 vs published 18.27, 7.58) is unaffected. The item text shipped here does not depend on this. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv carries a 'ship' verdict for the Watson/Clark/Tellegen PANAS (2026-09-08, batch_098; no fee, permission, NC or no-redistribution clause locatable -- a bare journal copyright notice is not a term on the instrument); applied here, not re-derived. Variant check per that row: 20 items, 1-5 scale, 10/10 PA/NA split -- the original PANAS, not PANAS-X (60) or I-PANAS-SF (10). The paper and deposit are CC BY 4.0.
public_note: Item text for this Czech-administered PANAS table is the canonical English Watson, Clark & Tellegen (1988) adjectives and response anchors, not the Czech wording respondents read, which the study does not publish; the adjectives are assigned by the canonical item order, which the data confirm to the level of positive/negative subscale (with 'alert' behaving like a negative-affect item in this sample, as the authors note) but which nothing in the source confirms item by item within a subscale.

source_ref: Sanford K, Elkins G (2024) Psychological Assessment 36(10):631-642, doi:10.1037/pas0001336 (PMC11866838 Tables 1-2); OSF osf.io/4td6k: '2024 Sanford SPSS variable definitions.pdf' (osf.io/download/5n9aj), '2024 Sanford EWAS Study 1.sav' (kdngt), '2024 Sanford EWAS Study 2.sav' (yw79x); data/EWAS_Sanford_2024.R
note: Words AND mapping from the study's own OSF deposit (osf.io/4td6k, node licence CC-By Attribution 4.0 International, copyright holder Keith Sanford): '2024 Sanford SPSS variable definitions.pdf' (osf.io/download/5n9aj) prints every Study 1 variable name Mea1..Prod6 beside its full stem and its coded options, e.g. 'Mea3 mea3 Doing something meaningful means ... Much more than an average person (7) ... Much less than an average person (1)'; all 30 stems and 180 option rows transcribed verbatim from it (pdftotext, line-wrap joins only), including the source's own per-item variants (sat4 options 3/1 read 'I can list one or two things' / 'No, I cannot think of anything' where the other type-4 items read 'I can list at least one thing' / 'No, I cannot list anything'; prod6 keeps the source's 'to accomplish things or made progress toward goals'). The Study 1 .sav (osf.io/download/kdngt) carries NO variable or value labels; the Study 2 .sav (osf.io/download/yw79x) labels its 6 EWAS columns and those variable labels and value labels match the codebook text character-for-character (6/6, all options). CODE DERIVATION: data/EWAS_Sanford_2024.R selects Mea1..Prod6 (Study 1) and prod1,enri2,enga3,sat1,mea2,enri3 (Study 2) BY NAME and lowercases, so the IRW code IS the source column name; mapping_basis is paper_explicit rather than data_labels only because for 24 of 30 items the name-to-text tie is printed in the study's companion codebook, not in the .sav itself. STEP 3b: live table = 30 items, resp 1..7, matching the paper's 30-item Study 1 pool (5 appraisal domains x 6 response formats) plus the 6-item final EWAS in Study 2; the Flourishing Scale columns are the separate sibling table. Paper Table 1 prints abbreviated EXAMPLE items per format (its type 5 reads 'During this last week, did this happen for you? ...'), which differ from the administered wording; the codebook, which matches the data file, was used, not Table 1. instructions and section_prompt blank: no instruction text is reproduced in the codebook, .sav or paper (items were presented in random order in three blocks of 10 in Study 1). RIGHTS: EWAS is Sanford's own instrument. No fee, permission requirement, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause located: the paper (PMC11866838, NIH author manuscript) states none, the OSF deposit is CC BY 4.0, and Sanford's Baylor lab page (psychologyneuroscience.artsandsciences.baylor.edu/interpersonal-relationships-and-health-laboratory-dr-keith-sanford, fetched 2026-09-18) offers no scales and states no terms. Silence is permission, so it ships; no register row written (a round may not write ship rows). Distinct from the blocked sibling EWAS_Sanford_2024_Flourish, whose block rests on Diener's NC clause for the Flourishing Scale; that clause does not reach EWAS.
